chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A wound may be in a place that we are unable to bandage, so blood and pus flow from it and come onto my garment. He said: “Leave it, and it does not harm you not to wash it.”

key_terms.تَغْسِلَهُ: to wash it, referring to the stained garment
key_terms.رَبْطِهِ: bandaging or tying it to contain the wound
key_terms.فَلَا يَضُرُّكَ: it does not harm you, meaning there is no legal blame or consequence

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if blood and pus from an unbandageable wound stain one's clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding impurity from a wound that cannot be practically bandaged or contained. Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام states that if blood and pus from such a wound reach one's garment, there is no harm in leaving it without washing, indicating legal concession in cases of hardship.
